role: The program's C entry point: verifies the installation and the CD-ROM, reads the Disk.no file, switches to VGA mode 13h, then runs the top-level game state loop until the quit flag is set and restores text mode on the way out.
plate_comment:
C entry point of FDPS. Called by the Watcom startup routine at 0004df4c, which pushes _argc (0006a3b4) and _argv (0006a3b8) and passes this function's return value to exit().

Algorithm:
  1. access("DISK.NO", 0) via INT 21h AH=43h. A non-zero result means the game was
     never installed: print "\nCan't found file 'Disk.No' !!!\a\n" and
     "Please use install function.\n", then exit(1).
  2. fopen("Disk.no", "rt"), three fscanf(fp, "%s", ...) reads and fclose(). The first
     two tokens go to a stack buffer and are discarded; the third is stored in the
     global string buffer at 000643e8. Sets the global at 00069d54 to -1.
  3. Calls the CD-ROM presence check at 0003c636 (returns a 16-bit value, sign-extended
     by CWDE). Anything other than 1 prints
     "Fatal error: CDROM is not install!!!\a\n" and "Check your CDROM please!!!\n",
     then exit(1).
  4. Subsystem init: 000304e0(0x19) and 00029660(), then int386(0x10, &regs, &regs)
     with regs.ax = 0x13 to enter VGA 320x200x256 mode.
  5. Clears the state globals (00069cf0, 00069cdc, 00069da0) and the quit flag at
     000643eb, calls 0002a2b0() once, then loops while the quit flag is zero:
       - 0002bae0() pumps one iteration;
       - the request code left in 00069da0 is dispatched: 0 does nothing, 1 runs
         0002a960() followed by 0002a2b0(), 2 calls the handler taken from the
         function-pointer table at 00060304 indexed by the mode selector in 00069cf4
         and then 00031210();
       - the request code is reset to 0 at the end of every iteration.
  6. Shutdown: 00029440(), 000305a0(), 0003c4a7() (pairs with the CD check),
     int386(0x10, &regs, &regs) with regs.ax = 3 to return to text mode, and finally
     prints "\nThank you for playing Flame Dragon Plus!! \n\n".

Parameters:
  argc, argv - passed on the stack by the startup code but never read by this function.

Returns:
  Nothing meaningful. Control falls off the end of the function, so EAX holds whatever
  the final print call left there; the startup code feeds it to exit(). In C source
  terms this is a main() with no return statement.
params: Frame is PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP; MOV EBP,ESP; SUB ESP,0x3c, so incoming arguments would live at [EBP+0x14] and [EBP+0x18] - neither is ever referenced. No register is read before being written: EAX, ECX and EDX are all written before use, and EBX/ESI/EDI are only saved and restored. The caller at 0004df8f pushes two dwords and cleans them up itself with ADD ESP,0x8, so this is a stack-argument, caller-purge (__cdecl) signature of the shape int main(int argc, char **argv), with both parameters unused. Ghidra's decompiler invents param_1/param_2 and an unaff_EBX; all three are artifacts.
evidence:
Caller 0004df4c is the Watcom C startup: it computes the stack size from 00060438, calls the initialisation chain, pushes the globals at 0006a3b4/0006a3b8 (argc/argv), calls this function and passes the result straight to exit (00042e0f) - the canonical __CMain -> main -> exit shape, and 0004df4c is this function's only caller. String evidence, read directly out of .data: 00061be0 "DISK.NO", 00061be8 "
Can't found file 'Disk.No' !!!\a
", 00061c0c "Please use install function.
", 00061c2c "rt", 00061c30 "Disk.no", 00061c38 "%s", 00061c3c "Fatal error: CDROM is not install!!!\a
", 00061c64 "Check your CDROM please!!!
", 00061c80 "
Thank you for playing Flame Dragon Plus!! 

" - the last one names the game and is the program's final output. CRT primitives identified by reading them: 00042438 is access() (INT 21h AH=43h get-attributes on the EDX filename, error funnelled through 0004bd13); 0004265e is fopen (name, mode); 00043243 is fscanf (stream, format, buffer); 000428be is fclose; 00042deb is the single-argument print used for every message; 00042e0f is exit; 00043268 is int386 - it reserves a 12-byte segment-register block, fills it via 0004df22 and forwards intno/in/out plus that block to int386x at 00043657, and both call sites here pass intno 0x10 with a local union REGS whose ax field is set to 0x13 then 3, i.e. the VGA mode-13h enter/exit pair. Data touched: 00069d54 (set to -1), 000643e8 (destination of the third Disk.no token), 000643eb (quit flag polled by the loop), 00069cf0 / 00069cdc / 00069da0 (state and request-code globals), 00069cf4 indexing the function-pointer table at 00060304.
cc_note: This is the one function in the binary that is expected not to use the __watcall register default: the Watcom startup calls main with stack-passed arguments and cleans them up itself (ADD ESP,0x8 after the call), so the correct convention here is __cdecl. Do not let a global "everything is __watcall" pass rewrite it.
open_question: The quit flag at 000643eb sits three bytes after the buffer at 000643e8 that receives the third "%s" token scanned from Disk.no. Whether these are two independent globals or the flag is byte 3 of a small buffer could not be settled from this function alone; at runtime it does not matter, because the flag is explicitly zeroed after the file is read, but it needs deciding before the buffer gets a declared size in the rebuilt source. Also unresolved: what the three whitespace-separated tokens in the Disk.no file mean and why only the third is kept.

role: Watcom C runtime `exit()`: runs the first two runtime finalizer hooks, then tail-calls the `_exit` stage with the same status code, terminating the program.
plate_comment:
C runtime exit().

Algorithm:
  Calls two runtime finalizer hooks indirectly through the function-pointer
  slots at 0x000603a0 and 0x000603a4, then pushes its own status argument and
  calls the next termination stage at 0x00042e29 (_exit), cleaning the argument
  off the stack afterwards.

  The three adjacent slots 0x000603a0 / 0x000603a4 / 0x000603a8 form the
  runtime's finalizer hook table. exit() runs slots [0] and [1]; the _exit
  stage at 0x00042e29 runs slots [1] and [2] and then jumps into the cstart
  termination tail at 0x00043527, which pops the status into EAX and reaches
  INT 21h AH=4Ch. In this build all three slots are statically initialised to
  0x00042e0e, a bare RET stub, i.e. no finalizer module was linked in, so the
  hooks are effectively no-ops.

  The trailing RET is unreachable: control never comes back from 0x00042e29.
  This function does not return.

Parameters:
  [ESP+4]  int status - process exit code, forwarded unchanged to _exit and
           ultimately to the DOS terminate call.

Returns:
  Does not return.
params: The only input is the stack slot [ESP+4], read at 00042e1b into EDX. No register is read before being written, so nothing arrives in EAX/EDX/EBX/ECX. The function ends with a plain RET (no stack purge); the call site in __CMain at 0004df97 does PUSH EAX / CALL 0x00042e0f / ADD ESP,0x4, so the caller cleans the argument. That is one int argument passed on the stack, caller-cleaned: __cdecl, not the __watcall default.
evidence:
Body is 7 instructions: CALL [0x000603a0]; CALL [0x000603a4]; MOV EDX,[ESP+4]; PUSH EDX; CALL 0x00042e29; ADD ESP,4; RET.

Caller context is decisive. FUN_0004df4c is Watcom's __CMain: it computes the stack size from DAT_00060438, calls the init-routine chain at 0x00054dbc, then does MOV EDX,[0x0006a3b8]; PUSH EDX; MOV EBX,[0x0006a3b4]; PUSH EBX; CALL 0x00029220 (argv/envp pointers -> main); ADD ESP,8; PUSH EAX; CALL 0x00042e0f. That is literally `exit( main( argc, argv, envp ) )`, which fixes this function as exit() and 0x00029220 as main. __CMain itself is reached from the cstart stub at 0x00043522 (the INT 21h AH=30h / DPMI "DX"/"CB"/INT 31h startup block at 0x00043310).

Callee chain confirms termination: 0x00042e29 calls hooks [0x000603a4] and [0x000603a8], pushes the same status, and JMPs to 0x00043527, which does POP EAX and falls into 0x0004354d -> PUSH EAX; ... ; POP EAX; MOV AH,0x4C; INT 0x21 (DOS terminate-with-return-code). So the status pushed here ends up as the DOS exit code.

Data evidence: read_memory at 0x00060398 gives 00 00 00 00 | 01 00 00 00 | 0e 2e 04 00 | 0e 2e 04 00 | 0e 2e 04 00, i.e. slots 0x603a0/0x603a4/0x603a8 all hold 0x00042e0e, and 0x00042e0e disassembles to a single RET. No code anywhere writes those three slots (get_xrefs_to shows only the two READ references from 00042e0f and the two from 00042e29), so they are link-time-initialised finalizer hooks left at the empty default. Neighbouring slots in the same block are cstart's own globals (0x000603ac is written by the DOS/4G startup at 0x00043398, 0x000603b0 stores the GS selector at 0x000433e3), placing this table squarely in the runtime data area.

Caller count also fits exit(): 11 callers = __CMain (0x0004df4c), main itself (0x00029220), and 9 scattered game functions (0x000177d0, 0x00017ca0, 0x0001a4c0, 0x00023e20, 0x00029400, 0x00029660, 0x0002a140, 0x0002a240, 0x0002e640) — the shape of fatal-error bail-outs, not of a game-logic helper.

No strings are referenced; none are expected for this routine.
cc_note: Deviates from the __watcall default. The single int argument is read from [ESP+4] with no register inputs, and the callee returns with a plain RET while the caller does ADD ESP,0x4 — __cdecl, caller-cleaned. Prototype should be `void __cdecl crt_exit(int status)`. It should additionally be flagged no-return: the RET at 00042e28 is unreachable because 0x00042e29 tail-jumps into the DOS terminate path.
open_question: The exact upstream Watcom names of the three finalizer hook slots (0x000603a0 / 0x000603a4 / 0x000603a8) cannot be recovered from this binary — all three hold the same empty RET stub, so nothing distinguishes them here. Which upstream stage each slot corresponds to (atexit dispatch, stdio flush/close, low-level cleanup) would have to be settled against the Watcom 10.0a clib sources, not against FDPS.LE. Note also that slot 0x000603a4 is run twice on the exit() path (once here, once inside 0x00042e29); whether that is genuine or whether one of the two is a different priority band is unresolved for the same reason.

role: The LE module entry point: a single short jump that skips over the inline Watcom copyright banner and runtime data words to reach the real C runtime startup code at 00043310.
plate_comment:
LE module entry point (Watcom cstart_.asm).

Algorithm:
  The whole body is one 2-byte instruction, JMP 0x00043310 (EB 76). The 0x76
  bytes it jumps over are data, not code: the ASCII banner "WATCOM C/C++32
  Run-Time system. (c) Copyright by WATCOM International Corp. 1988-1994. All
  rights reserved." at 0004329A, a 3-byte LEA EAX,[EAX+0] pad, the runtime
  version/flag words 0003 0001, and the default console device name "con" at
  0004330C. Control lands on the startup body at 00043310, which begins
  STI / AND ESP,-4 / MOV EBX,ESP, identifies the DOS extender (RSX 'DX',
  'CB', or DPMI via INT 21h AX=FF00 'PHAR'), shrinks the DOS memory block,
  records PSP/environment pointers, copies the command tail, scans the
  environment for the "no87=" variable, clears BSS, runs the initialiser
  chain and finally exits through INT 21h AH=4Ch.

  This stub exists only so the entry address can sit immediately before the
  banner that the linker embeds; it is emitted by the Watcom startup object
  linked in by wlink and has no counterpart in hand-written C.

Parameters:
  None. Execution arrives here from the LE header's initial CS:EIP, set up by
  the DOS/4G loader; nothing is passed in registers or on the stack by any
  caller inside the image. Ghidra's six-parameter signature is an artifact of
  the decompiler inlining the jump target.

Returns:
  Does not return. The startup path it enters terminates the process with
  INT 21h AH=4Ch.
params: The body is a single JMP; it reads no register, writes no register, touches no memory and performs no stack adjustment, so the disassembly gives no parameter evidence at all. There is no prologue, no argument register read before write (EAX/EDX/EBX/ECX are all untouched here), no stack-relative access and no RET, hence no stack purge. The six parameters and the undefined4 return in the current signature come from Ghidra decompiling the jump target's code under this symbol; they are not real. The correct prototype is a no-argument, non-returning entry.
evidence: get_entry_points reports "_entry @ 00043298 [Function] (6 params) [external entry]" and get_xrefs_to returns only "From Entry Point [EXTERNAL]" — no code inside the image calls it. read_memory at 00043298 gives EB 76 (short JMP to 0x4329A+0x76 = 0x43310) followed directly by the literal ASCII string "WATCOM C/C++32 Run-Time system. (c) Copyright by WATCOM International Corp. 1988-1994. All rights reserved.", then 8D 40 00, the words 03 00 01 00, and "con\0" at 0004330C — the exact data layout Watcom's cstart_.asm places between the entry label and the startup body. The jump target 00043310 begins FB 83 E4 FC 89 E3 (STI; AND ESP,-4; MOV EBX,ESP), and the decompilation of the target shows the Watcom extender-detection sequence (INT 21h with AX values compared against 0x4458 and 0x4243, INT 21h AX=FF00 with the 'PHAR' signature 0x50484152, INT 31h AX=0006), the PSP command-tail copy from offset 0x81, the "no87=" environment scan (compare of *p|0x20202020 against 0x37386F6E followed by '='), a BSS clear of 0x6a8c bytes from 0x63930, and termination via INT 21h AH=4Ch. The 1988-1994 copyright range matches Watcom 10.x, consistent with the project's toolchain determination.
cc_note: No calling convention applies. This is the image entry point reached from the LE header's initial EIP, never called by C code, and it does not return (the path it enters exits via INT 21h AH=4Ch). The current __watcall signature with six parameters and an undefined4 return is wrong and is purely an artifact of Ghidra folding the jump target into this 2-byte symbol; the honest prototype is void crt_cstart(void) marked no-return.
open_question: Whether the orchestrator wants this 2-byte stub kept as its own function or absorbed into the startup function at 00043310 — in the original source they are one contiguous piece of assembly in Watcom's cstart_ object, split here only because the banner data sits between them. Also unresolved from this function alone: this code is supplied by the Watcom startup object at link time, so it has no hand-written C counterpart in src/ and should not be reimplemented.

role: Watcom C runtime startup entry: detects the DOS extender host, resizes/records memory and selectors, builds the command line and program name from the PSP and environment, zeroes BSS, runs the initializer table, then calls __CMain (which calls main and exit).
plate_comment:
Watcom C/C++ 10.0a runtime startup code (cstrt386.asm, _cstart_). This is the
real program entry: the LE entry stub at 00043298 is a bare JMP to here. Hand
written assembly, not compiled C.

Algorithm:
  1. STI, align ESP down to a dword boundary, and record the initial stack
     pointer in the runtime globals at 00060434 and 00060420. Preload the
     default selector 0x24 into 0006042c and EBX with 'PHAR' for the Phar Lap
     probe.
  2. INT 21h AH=30h (get DOS version). AL/AH are stored as the DOS major and
     minor version at 00060457 and 00060458. The high half of EAX selects the
     host:
       - 'DX'  (0x4458): Phar Lap 386|DOS-Extender. Take the version digit from
         BL, read the PSP memory-block end at ES:[5Ch] via selector 0006042c,
         round it up to a 4K boundary, store it at 00060420 and shrink the
         block with INT 21h AH=4Ah. Environment selector 0x2C.
       - 'CB'  (0x4243): Intel Code Builder. EDX points at the Code Builder
         info block; it is saved at 000603ac. Shrink memory by the amount at
         [EDX+1Ch] (INT 21h AH=4Ah), take the PSP pointer from [EDX+10h] (the
         command tail therefore starts at PSP+81h) and the environment segment
         from [PSP+2Ch], shifted left by 4.
       - otherwise: INT 21h AX=FF00h with DX=78h. If it reports a host, this is
         a DPMI/DOS-4G style extender: the GS selector, when non-zero, is saved
         at 000603b0, INT 31h AX=0006h fetches the DS segment base, the PSP
         selector is taken from ES and the environment selector from ES:[2Ch].
         If it reports nothing, fall back to the fixed real-mode-ish selectors
         (PSP 0x24, environment 0x2C, flat data 0x17).
     The resulting host type/subtype byte pair is written to 0006044e/0006044f,
     the environment pointer to 00060451 and its selector to 00060455.
  3. Self-modifying step: with the flat data selector in ES, store DS into the
     code at 0004356d, which is the operand of the "MOV DS,CS:[4356Dh]"
     instruction in the exit path at 00043564.
  4. Command line: read the tail length from PSP:80h, skip leading spaces with
     REPE SCASB, and copy the remaining tail with REP MOVSB to the 16-byte
     aligned buffer just past the end of BSS (0006a3bc rounded up), then append
     two NUL bytes. The buffer address is kept in 00060428.
  5. Environment scan: walk the environment strings; a string whose first four
     bytes lowercase to "no87" and whose fifth byte is '=' increments the
     no-x87 flag stored at 0006044c. After the terminating double NUL, skip the
     word count and copy the program name that follows to the end of the
     command line buffer; the pointer past it is stored at 00060430. The stack
     pointer is also recorded at 0006041c.
  6. Zero BSS from 00063930 up to 0006a3bc with REP STOSD plus a byte tail.
     When the host type byte at 0006044e is 1 (the DPMI path, where the loader
     already zero-fills the image) the cleared span is clamped to 0x1000 bytes.
     The aligned end of BSS is then stored at 00060424 as the heap/break base.
  7. Call __InitRtns (0004dfa6) with EAX=0FFh to run every registered
     initializer up to priority 255, clear EBP, then call __CMain (0004df4c),
     which sets up the stack limit, builds argc/argv and calls main (00029220),
     then exit (00042e0f). __CMain therefore never returns; the POP EAX / JMP
     00043528 tail that follows it only executes on paths that reach the shared
     exit sequence at 0004354d, which runs __FiniRtns (0004dff1) with
     EAX=0, EDX=0FFh and terminates with INT 21h AH=4Ch.

Parameters: none at the C level. The only incoming register state that is read
is supplied by the extender/loader: EDX (Intel Code Builder info block) and GS
(DPMI). The incoming stack contents are not used; ESP is only realigned and
recorded.

Returns: never returns. Control leaves through main/exit inside __CMain, or
through the INT 21h AH=4Ch terminate in the shared exit tail at 0004354d.
params: No argument is read off the stack: the first thing the function does is AND ESP,0xfffffffc and record ESP, so incoming stack contents are ignored, and there is no stack purge because the function never executes a RET. Of the registers, EAX, EBX, ECX, ESI, EDI and EBP are all written before they are read. Only two registers are read before being written, and both are loader-supplied rather than C arguments: EDX in the Intel Code Builder branch (00043398 MOV [000603ac],EDX / MOV ESI,EDX, then [ESI+1Ch], [ESI+10h]) and GS in the DPMI branch (000433da MOV AX,GS). Ghidra's six __watcall parameters are decompiler invention: param_5/param_6 are just the realigned stack slots and param_2 is the EDX described above.
evidence: Structural: the LE external entry _entry at 00043298 is a single JMP to 00043310, and this is the function's only xref, so it is the program entry. Algorithm shape is a byte-for-byte match for Watcom's cstrt386.asm _cstart_: INT 21h AH=30h with EBX preloaded to 0x50484152 ('PHAR') and the high-half comparisons against 0x4458 ('DX', Phar Lap 386|DOS-Extender) and 0x4243 ('CB', Intel Code Builder), the INT 21h AX=FF00h DX=78h host probe, INT 31h AX=0006h for the DPMI data-segment base, and INT 21h AH=4Ah memory shrink. The only ASCII constant in the body is 0x37386f6e ("no87") tested after OR EAX,0x20202020 with a following '=', i.e. the standard Watcom NO87 environment-variable check, whose result lands in the flag at 0006044c. Command line handling reads the PSP tail length at [EDI-1] with EDI=0x81 and copies it to a 16-byte-aligned buffer derived from 0006a3bc. Data addresses touched: 0006041c/00060420/00060424/00060428/00060430/00060434 (stack, break and command-line/program-name pointers), 0006042c (PSP selector), 0006044c (no87), 0006044e/0006044f (host type/subtype), 00060451/00060455 (environment pointer/selector), 00060457/00060458 (DOS major/minor from AH=30h), 000603ac (Code Builder block), 000603b0 (GS selector), and the code word at 0004356d that it patches with DS. Callees confirm the identity: 0004dfa6 walks the descriptor table 000638f0..00063920 in 6-byte records selecting entries by priority byte and calling [rec+2] - that is __InitRtns, invoked here with EAX=0FFh; 0004df4c sets a stack limit, then pushes [0006a3b8] and [0006a3b4] (argv, argc), calls 00029220 and passes its return value to 00042e0f - that is __CMain calling main and exit. The shared tail at 0004354d calls 0004dff1 with EAX=0/EDX=0FFh (__FiniRtns) and terminates with INT 21h AH=4Ch.
cc_note: Deviates from the __watcall default: this is hand-written assembly with no C calling convention at all. It takes no parameters, never returns, and must not be typed as __watcall with six arguments. The correct prototype is a no-return void function (void __cdecl/no-args, marked no-return in Ghidra); its only inputs are the EDX and GS values the DOS extender leaves in place at entry.
open_question: The individual runtime globals are identified by role from the code, but their canonical Watcom CRT names (which of 0006041c/00060420/00060424/00060428/00060430/00060434 is _STACKTOP vs _curbrk vs _LpCmdLine vs _LpPgmName, and whether 0006044e/0006044f is the __Extender/__ExtenderSubtype pair) were not cross-checked against a Watcom 10.0a library build. Also unverified: why the DPMI path clamps the BSS clear to 0x1000 bytes - it is presumed to be the loader-zero-fills-the-image case, but that was not confirmed against the LE image's BSS declaration.

role: Watcom CRT startup routine that calibrates the busy-wait loop used by delay(), by counting how many INT 21h AH=2Ch calls fit into one wall-clock second and storing the count at 0x00069ea8.
plate_comment:
Watcom C runtime initialiser: calibrate the delay() busy-wait loop.

Algorithm:
  Phase 1 (sync): issue DOS "Get System Time" (INT 21h, AH=2Ch; returns
  CH=hour, CL=minute, DH=second, DL=hundredths), keep the seconds field
  (DH), then re-issue the call until DH changes. This aligns the
  measurement with a whole-second boundary so no partial second is
  counted.
  Phase 2 (count): with the new seconds value latched in BL, spin issuing
  INT 21h AH=2Ch and incrementing a counter until DH changes again. The
  counter therefore holds the number of INT 21h AH=2Ch round trips this
  machine performs in one second.
  The result is stored to the global at 0x00069ea8. delay() at 0x00043cb0
  is its only consumer: it computes
  iterations = (milliseconds * [0x00069ea8] + 500) / 1000, clamps a zero
  result up to 1, and spins that many INT 21h AH=2Ch calls. The stored
  value is thus "loop iterations per 1000 ms" on the host CPU.

  The routine is not reached by a CALL. It is entry 0 of the Watcom
  runtime init table at 0x000638f0 (6-byte records: status byte,
  priority byte, 32-bit routine address); its record reads
  00 20 82 3C 04 00 - status 0 (pending), priority 0x20
  (INIT_PRIORITY_LIBRARY), routine 0x00043C82. The table walker at
  0x0004DFA6 invokes it during startup and then marks the record 2 (done).

Parameters:
  None. EBX and ESI are pushed on entry and popped on exit; every other
  register the body reads (EAX, EDX) is written by INT 21h before being
  used, so no incoming register or stack argument exists.

Returns:
  void. The calibration result is delivered through the global at
  0x00069ea8. Stack is balanced by a plain RET (no purge).
params: Takes no parameters and returns nothing. Disassembly shows EBX and ESI saved with PUSH at entry and restored with POP before RET, so they are callee-saved, not inputs. Every register read in the body (AL/DH from EDX, EAX) is first written by the INT 21h AH=2Ch call, so nothing live-in is consumed. No [ESP+n] access at all, and the function ends with a bare RET (0-byte purge). Ghidra's decompiled signature FUN_00043c82(undefined4 param_1, uint param_2) is an artefact of the decompiler modelling INT 21h as an indirect call through swi(0x21); param_2 is just its stand-in for EDX loaded by the interrupt. Correct prototype: void __watcall crt_init_delay(void).
evidence: 1. INT 21h AH=2Ch is the DOS Get System Time service (CH=hour, CL=minute, DH=second, DL=hundredths). The body only ever reads DH, i.e. the seconds field, which identifies this as wall-clock timing rather than a time-of-day query. 2. The two-phase shape - wait for a second boundary, then count service calls until the next boundary - is the textbook one-second calibration loop. 3. The single reader of the global it writes, 0x00069ea8, is FUN_00043cb0 at 0x00043cba, which is a verbatim Watcom delay(): it reads the arg from [ESP+0xC], computes (ms * calibration + 0x1F4) / 0x3E8 (i.e. round-to-nearest division by 1000), forces a zero result up to 1 via LEA ESI,[EAX+1], and spins that many INT 21h AH=2Ch calls. That fixes the stored value's unit as iterations per 1000 ms. get_xrefs_to 0x00069ea8 returns exactly two references: this WRITE and that READ, so the global is private to the delay pair - the classic single-translation-unit static in Watcom's dos/c/delay.c. 4. The lone "caller" FUN_0004DFA6 is not a real call site but the Watcom runtime init-table walker: it scans 0x000638F0..0x00063920 in 6-byte strides, skips records whose first byte is already 2, picks the lowest priority byte, CALLs the 32-bit address at record+2, then stamps the record with 2. Reading 0x000638F0 gives the first record as 00 20 82 3C 04 00 - pending, priority 0x20, routine 0x00043C82 - so this function is registered as a library-priority startup initialiser (Watcom's AXI/INIT_PRIORITY_LIBRARY = 32 registration), which is precisely how delay()'s calibration hook is wired in the Watcom CRT. 5. No strings, no game data addresses, no float or graphics work - nothing ties it to game logic; the only state it touches is the delay pair's own global.
cc_note: Nothing deviates from the __watcall default. EBX/ESI are preserved as the Watcom register convention requires, EAX/EDX are treated as scratch, and the RET has no stack purge. The only unusual thing is dispatch: it is never the target of a CALL instruction in the code, it is reached indirectly through the runtime init table at 0x000638F0, so the prototype must be void(void) - there are no register arguments that a wrong signature could silently invent.
open_question: FUN_00043cb0, the delay() that consumes this calibration, shows no direct callers in Ghidra. Either it is invoked through a pointer, from a region not yet analysed as code, or the whole delay module was pulled in by the linker only because the init-table record references this initialiser. Worth settling later, because it decides whether the calibration is live behaviour or dead library baggage in the rebuild. Not investigated further here - that is a different function.

role: Watcom CRT `__CMain`: reserves the auto-stack block, runs `__CommonInit`, then calls `main(_argc, _argv)` and hands its return value to `exit`.
plate_comment:
Watcom C/C++ 10.0a CRT routine __CMain, from library module cmain386 (CLIB3S.LIB).
Byte-identical to the library copy; the externs it references are, in order,
__ASTACKSIZ, stackavail, __ASTACKPTR, __CommonInit, ___Argv, ___Argc, main, exit.

Algorithm:
  1. Load __ASTACKSIZ (0x00060438), round it up to a multiple of 4 ((n + 3) & ~3,
     coded as ADD EBX,3 / AND BL,0FCh).
  2. Call stackavail (0x0004e692, ESP - __STACKLOW at 0x00060430). If the rounded
     size is smaller than the free stack, carve the block off the stack with
     SUB ESP,size and keep the resulting ESP as the block base; otherwise use a
     null base, i.e. no auto-stack is reserved.
  3. Store base + __ASTACKSIZ (the unrounded size) into __ASTACKPTR (0x0006043c).
     In this build __ASTACKSIZ is 0 and __ASTACKPTR is never read back, so the
     whole step is inert here.
  4. Call __CommonInit (0x00054dbc), which sets _amblksiz (0x000613c4) to 0x8000.
  5. Push _argv (0x0006a3b8) then _argc (0x0006a3b4), call main (0x00029220),
     clean the two arguments off the stack, then push main's return value and
     call exit (0x00042e0f).

Control never comes back: exit runs the atexit/fini chains and terminates. The
epilogue (MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP / POP EBX / RET) exists only to restore the frame
and the saved EBX and is unreachable in practice.

The single caller is the DOS/4G CRT startup at 0x00043310, which invokes
__InitRtns(255) at 0x0004dfa6, then this function, then __FiniRtns(0,255) at
0x0004dff1 before the INT 21h/AH=4Ch fallback.

Parameters: none. EBX and EBP are callee-saved here, not inputs; every other
register is written before it is read, and RET performs no stack purge.

Returns: nothing (void). The function does not return to its caller.
params: No parameters. The prologue is PUSH EBX / PUSH EBP / MOV EBP,ESP, and both saved registers are restored at the end, so EBX/EBP are preserved rather than read as arguments. EAX, EBX and EDX are all written before any read; nothing is loaded from [EBP+n] or [ESP+n]. The function ends in a bare RET with no stack purge. Ghidra already types it `void __watcall FUN_0004df4c(void)`, which is correct; the decompiler's `extraout_EAX` is an artefact of it mis-ordering the argument pushes for the call to main.
evidence: Positive library identification. The relocation-free run 39c3730889d829c489e0eb0231c0 (the stackavail comparison, the SUB ESP alloca and the XOR EAX,EAX else-branch) is found in CLIB3R.LIB/CLIB3S.LIB of every installed Watcom, at 0x17a67 in WATCOM_10.0a\LIB386\DOS\CLIB3S.LIB (checked with tools/build_flags/lib_bytematch.py). Dumping the OMF records around that offset gives module name `cmain386`, public symbol `__CMain`, and the extern list `__ASTACKSIZ`, `stackavail`, `__ASTACKPTR`, `__CommonInit`, `___Argv`, `___Argc`, `main`, `exit` — a one-to-one match with the disassembly: 0x00060438 = __ASTACKSIZ, 0x0004e692 = stackavail (MOV EAX,ESP / SUB EAX,[0x00060430] / RET, i.e. ESP - __STACKLOW), 0x0006043c = __ASTACKPTR, 0x00054dbc = __CommonInit (sets _amblksiz at 0x000613c4 to 0x8000; the preceding library module `cinit` publishes both __CommonInit and _amblksiz), 0x0006a3b4 = _argc, 0x0006a3b8 = _argv, 0x00029220 = main, 0x00042e0f = exit (which calls the two chain pointers at 0x000603a0/0x000603a4 before terminating). Caller context agrees: the only caller, 0x00043310, is the DOS/4G CRT startup (INT 21h AH=30h/AH=4Ah, the 'DX'/'CB'/DPMI host probes, PSP command-line and environment copy, BSS clear) and calls __InitRtns / this / __FiniRtns in that order. 0x00060438 is initialised data outside the BSS-clear range and is never written by any instruction — its value is 0, so no auto-stack block is actually reserved in this build; 0x0006043c is written here and read nowhere.
cc_note: Nothing unusual for the function itself: zero parameters, void return, no stack purge — indistinguishable from and compatible with the __watcall default. It should additionally be marked no-return, since control leaves through exit. Two secondary observations for the calling-convention work: this routine passes main's arguments on the stack (PUSH argv / PUSH argc / CALL / ADD ESP,8, caller cleanup) rather than in registers, which is the CLIB3S (stack-convention) form of cmain386 and matches the module found in CLIB3S.LIB; and 0x0004e692 (stackavail) returns its value in EAX with no arguments, so it too gives no register-convention signal.
open_question: What sets __ASTACKSIZ (0x00060438) is not visible: no instruction writes it and its image value is 0, so it must come from the link (a wlink/CRT-supplied absolute or a data definition pulled from the library). Confirming that it is genuinely 0 at run time would let the whole auto-stack block be treated as dead code when the CRT is re-emitted.

role: Watcom C runtime __InitRtns: repeatedly scans the linker-built XI initialiser table at 0x638f0..0x63920, calling the not-yet-run entry with the lowest priority (bounded by the argument) until none is left.
plate_comment:
Watcom C runtime __InitRtns -- run the link-time initialiser table.

Algorithm:
The linker gathers records of the form

    struct rt_init { unsigned char rtn_type;      /* 2 == already run */
                     unsigned char priority;
                     void (*rtn)( void ); };      /* 6 bytes each */

into a contiguous "XI" table. Here that table spans 0x000638f0
(inclusive) to 0x00063920 (exclusive), i.e. 8 entries; a matching
"YI" rundown table begins at 0x00063920 and is walked by the
termination routine at 0x0004dff1.

Outer loop, repeated until no candidate remains:
  - set the running minimum priority to the caller-supplied bound and
    the selected entry to the table end (the "nothing found" sentinel);
  - scan the whole table forward; an entry is a candidate when its
    rtn_type is not 2 (not yet executed) and its priority is <= the
    running minimum, in which case it becomes the new selection and
    lowers the minimum. Because the test is <= rather than <, a later
    entry with a priority equal to the current minimum displaces an
    earlier one, so entries sharing a priority execute in reverse
    table order;
  - if nothing was selected, return;
  - otherwise reload ES from DS, call the entry's function pointer
    when it is non-NULL, and stamp rtn_type = 2 so the entry is never
    run twice.

The current table holds eight entries, all rtn_type 0, with priorities
0x01 (0x0003d50a), 0x02 (0x00044749) and six at 0x20 (0x00043c82,
0x0004cfc8, 0x0004e040, 0x00043612, 0x00054893, 0x00054f86).

Parameters:
  EAX (only AL is used) -- the priority ceiling. Entries whose
  priority exceeds it are skipped. The startup code at 0x00043310
  passes 0xff, i.e. "run everything".

Returns:
  Nothing. ESI, EDI, EBX, EDX and the ES segment register are saved on
  entry and restored before returning.
params: One register argument. EAX is read before any write (MOV EDX,EAX at 0x4dfad, then MOV AL,DL at 0x4dfbb seeds the running priority minimum), and only its low byte AL participates in the CMP byte ptr [ESI+1],AL comparison. No stack arguments are touched: the function never reads [ESP+n] beyond its own pushes and ends with a bare RET (zero-byte purge). ESI, EDI, EBX, EDX and ES are pushed at 0x4dfa6..0x4dfaa and popped in reverse at 0x4dfeb..0x4dfef. No return value is produced (EAX holds a scratch function pointer at exit).
evidence: Structure matches Watcom's __InitRtns exactly: a 6-byte-record table (0x00063920 - 0x000638f0 = 0x30 = 8 records), record layout byte rtn_type / byte priority / dword function pointer, repeated lowest-priority-first selection, "already run" marker 2 written back after the call, and a NULL function-pointer guard. Raw table bytes at 0x638f0 decode to eight well-formed records whose pointers (0x0003d50a, 0x00043612, 0x00043c82, 0x00044749, 0x0004cfc8, 0x0004e040, 0x00054893, 0x00054f86) all land on real function entries, and whose rtn_type is 0 in every case -- an init table, not a rundown table. Ghidra independently records 0x00043c82 (the first record's pointer) as a computed callee of the CALL EAX at 0x4dfe3. The sole caller is the DOS/4G assembly startup at 0x00043310, which does MOV EAX,0xff / CALL 0x4dfa6 at 0x00043516 immediately after zeroing BSS (0x63930..0x6a3bc) and setting up _psp/_osmajor/argv, and immediately before CALL 0x0004df4c; that is the canonical cstrt386 sequence. The companion function at 0x0004dff1 walks the adjacent table starting at 0x00063920, i.e. the YI rundown table, which pins 0x638f0..0x63920 as the XI init table. The PUSH DS / POP ES before each indirect call and the PUSH ES / POP ES bracketing are the hand-written-assembly ES fixup found in Watcom's real-mode-derived startup code.
cc_note: Argument arrives in EAX and the function returns with a bare RET (no stack purge), which is consistent with the __watcall default for a single unsigned argument. It does however preserve EDX and the ES segment register, which __watcall does not require of a callee -- a C compiler emitting this signature would be free to clobber EDX. That, plus the segment manipulation, means this is a hand-written assembly runtime routine rather than compiled C; for the rebuild it should come from the Watcom library rather than be re-emitted as C.

role: Returns the number of bytes of stack space still available, computed as the current stack pointer minus the runtime's stack-low limit at 0x00060430.
plate_comment:
Watcom C runtime: stackavail() -- report remaining stack space.

Algorithm:
  Copies ESP into EAX and subtracts the global stack-low limit stored at
  0x00060430, then returns. Because ESP at function entry already points at
  this call's own return address, the reported figure is 4 bytes smaller than
  the space the caller actually has, which is conservative and harmless.
  The same 0x00060430 global is the limit used by the compiler-generated
  stack-overflow probe at 0x0004362d (which tests ESP-size against it) and is
  initialised by the startup code at 0x000434c0, confirming it is __STACKLOW
  rather than a stack base or margin constant.

  All three callers are CRT internals that use the result to choose between an
  on-stack scratch buffer and the heap: 0x0004df4c and 0x000556a9 both compare
  (size + 3) & ~3 against the return value before pointing their buffer at a
  local array or at NULL, and 0x00043ab4 (the DOS int 21h AH=40h write path
  with LF->CRLF translation) calls the stack-overflow handler at 0x0004364b
  when fewer than 0xB0 bytes remain and otherwise picks a 0x200-byte staging
  buffer when at least 0x230 bytes are free, falling back to 0x80 bytes.

Parameters:
  None. EAX is written before any register is read, and no argument register
  or stack slot is consumed.

Returns:
  EAX = bytes of stack remaining below the current stack pointer, as an
  unsigned value. Every caller treats it as unsigned.
params: Zero parameters. The first instruction writes EAX from ESP, so no incoming register (EAX/EDX/EBX/ECX) is read before being written, and nothing is loaded from [ESP+n]. The function ends in a plain RET with no immediate, so the stack purge is 0 -- consistent with a zero-argument __watcall function. Result is returned in EAX.
evidence: Body is exactly three instructions: MOV EAX,ESP / SUB EAX,[0x00060430] / RET. The global 0x00060430 has only three xrefs: a WRITE from startup code FUN_00043310 at 0x000434c0, a READ from the stack-overflow probe FUN_0004362d at 0x00043635 (CMP EAX,ESP / SUB EAX,ESP / NEG EAX / CMP EAX,[0x00060430] / JBE overflow -- i.e. it tests the post-allocation stack pointer against a floor), and this READ. That identifies 0x00060430 as the Watcom __STACKLOW limit and this function as ESP - __STACKLOW, the textbook body of Watcom's stackavail(). Caller usage corroborates: FUN_0004df4c and FUN_000556a9 both compute (needed_size + 3) & 0xfffffffc, compare it against this function's return value, and select a local array or NULL accordingly (alloca-or-heap decision); FUN_000556a9 is a printf-family formatter (calls the format walker FUN_0005600f and buffer allocator FUN_0003d383), and FUN_00043ab4 is the low-level write path issuing int 21h AH=40h, which calls the overflow routine FUN_0004364b when the result is below 0xB0 and sizes its CRLF staging buffer 0x200 vs 0x80 on a 0x230 threshold. All three callers are runtime library code, not game logic, which places this in the crt pool. No strings or imports are involved.
open_question: The exact upstream Watcom symbol is not pinned down by disassembly alone: this could be the public stackavail() from malloc.h or an internal helper that stackavail() wraps. Confirming would need a byte comparison against the Watcom 10.0a clib. Separately, the global 0x00060430 is still unnamed in Ghidra; it should be labelled as the runtime stack-low limit (__STACKLOW) by whoever owns the startup function FUN_00043310.
cc_note: Nothing unusual. Zero arguments, return in EAX, RET with no stack purge -- indistinguishable from the __watcall default and from cdecl at this arity, so the default convention applies.

role: Sets the Watcom C runtime heap-growth granularity variable `_amblksiz` (at 0x000613c4) to 32768 bytes, once, just before the startup code enters main.
plate_comment:
Watcom C runtime helper: install the default heap growth granularity.

Algorithm:
  Stores the constant 0x8000 (32768) into the global at 0x000613c4 and returns.
  That global is the Watcom CRT variable `_amblksiz`, the minimum amount by
  which the heap manager grows the heap when it has to ask the system for more
  memory. Identification of the global rests on two other users of it:
    - 0x0004442b (heap grow helper) clamps a requested growth amount up to
      `_amblksiz` (with the low bit masked off, the documented Watcom flag bit)
      and then rounds the result up to a 4 KiB page boundary.
    - 0x0005600f (Watcom __cenvarg, the DOS spawn/exec command line and
      environment block builder) saves the global, forces it to 16 while it
      allocates the tightly sized argument block, and restores it afterwards -
      the exact save/set-16/restore idiom of the library source.
  The image initialises the global to 16; this routine raises it to 32 KiB so
  that a DOS extender heap is grown in large chunks instead of many small
  extender calls. It is called from the CRT startup path (0x0004df4c, which
  sizes the stack, then calls main at 0x00029220 and passes its result to exit
  at 0x00042e0f), so it runs exactly once before user code starts.

Parameters:
  None. The function reads no register and no stack slot.

Returns:
  Nothing. Only the global at 0x000613c4 is modified; no register is written.
params: The body is a single MOV of an immediate into an absolute address followed by RET. No register is read before being written, nothing is read from the stack frame, there is no prologue and no stack purge on the RET (plain near RET, caller-clean by construction since nothing is passed). The signature is void(void); the caller at 0x0004df7c pushes nothing and cleans nothing.
evidence: Body: `MOV dword ptr [0x000613c4],0x8000; RET` (11 bytes, leaf, no callees). Single caller 0x0004df4c, which is CRT startup: it reads a size global 0x00060438, rounds it to 4, calls 0x0004e692 (`MOV EAX,ESP; SUB EAX,[0x00060430]; RET` = stack-available check against the stack-low global), optionally carves that much off ESP, stores the result to 0x0006043c, calls this function, then calls 0x00029220 with [0x0006a3b4] and [0x0006a3b8] as (argc, argv) and passes the return value to 0x00042e0f, which dispatches two global function pointers (fini/dtor tables at 0x000603a0/0x000603a4) before tail-calling 0x00042e29 - i.e. the caller is __CMain, 0x00029220 is main and 0x00042e0f is exit. The written global 0x000613c4 has only four other references, all consistent with Watcom `_amblksiz`: read at 0x00044472 inside a heap-grow routine that clamps the growth amount up to it (`AND BL,0xfe` strips the documented flag bit) and then page-aligns via `AND BH,0xf0 / XOR BL,BL`; and saved/set-to-16/restored at 0x00056062/0x00056068/0x000560a5/0x000560b7 inside 0x0005600f, which sums strlen (0x00042dd2) over a NULL-terminated string vector, allocates with 0x0003d383 falling back to 0x0003d375, rejects a command line longer than 0x7e bytes and writes 0x90 through an out-parameter - the Watcom DOS __cenvarg argument/environment block builder. Initial image value of the global is 0x00000010. Address neighbourhood (0x0003d000-0x00056000) is library code; game main sits far below at 0x00029220.
cc_note: Nothing deviates. A void(void) leaf that touches no register is indistinguishable between conventions, and the plain RET with no stack purge matches the __watcall default used everywhere else in this binary.
open_question: The exact upstream Watcom 10.0a symbol name for this one-line initialiser could not be confirmed from the binary alone (candidates such as __init_amblksiz / __InitAmblksiz); the proposed name is descriptive rather than verified against a library listing. Confirming it would need a dump of the Watcom 10.0a CLIB3R/CLIB3S object modules for a module whose only content is this store. Likewise the identification of 0x000613c4 as `_amblksiz` is inferred from usage, not from a symbol; the image default of 16 rather than the commonly cited 8192 is unexplained.
